name: 南墙戍营
The South Wall Garrison
before: 南墙根下扎着国舅府的戍营，营里戟士、弓手、铁骑都有，正往城门洞里运木头和铁锁，要把南门从里头封死。万国商馆的商人们打听到：春宴那天，南门要关，商馆要锁，第十二根杆子要锯，「一天之内，叫这城像十年前一样」。

At the foot of the south wall stands the Royal Uncle's garrison, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, hauling timber and iron locks into the gateway to seal the south gate from inside. The merchants of the Hall have learned the plan: on the day of the spring banquet the south gate shuts, the Hall is locked and the twelfth pole sawn down. 'In one day, make this city as it was ten years ago.'
after: 戍营散了，木头和铁锁扔进了护城河。营头的令箭上压着一张纸，是国舅的手令：「春宴之日，闭城三日。」纸背面还有一行，墨迹像是写完又想划掉，没划干净：「城里那个人，三日之内，要见分晓。」

The garrison scatters, its timber and locks thrown into the moat. Under the captain's command arrow is a sheet of paper, an order in the Royal Uncle's hand: 'On the day of the spring banquet, close the city for three days.' On the back is another line, the ink as if he wrote it and then tried to strike it out and didn't quite: 'That man in the city. Within three days, it will be settled.'

name: 扣货场
The Impound Yard
before: 城外一片用木栅圈起来的场子，叫「验货场」，进城的商队都要在这里「验货」，可验起来没完没了，有的验了一年还没验完。场里拴着几十峰骆驼，货堆上长了草。守场的是国舅府的人马，三路排开，验货的规矩就一条：交钱的先验。

A yard fenced with stakes outside the city, called the 'inspection yard'. Every caravan entering must have its goods inspected here, but the inspection never ends; some have waited a year and still aren't done. Dozens of camels are tethered inside and grass grows on the stacked goods. The Royal Uncle's forces guard it in three ranks, and the inspection has only one rule: those who pay are inspected first.
after: 守场的跑了，木栅推倒，商队一支支出了场。最后一支是从南边茶路上来的小马帮，扣了两年，马帮头子从怀里掏出一封信，封皮上写着「烦交丝路千里号账房」，落款只有一个「陆」字。「我们只交给他本人，」他说，「找了两年，城里没人认这个账房。」

The guards flee, the stakes are pushed down and the caravans file out one by one. The last is a small pack-horse train come up from the Tea Road in the south, held here two years. Its leader takes a letter from his coat. On the cover: 'Kindly deliver to the bookkeeper of the Qianli caravan, Silk Road.' It's signed with a single character: 'Lu'. 'We give it to him in person only,' he says. 'Two years we've searched. Nobody in the city knows any such bookkeeper.'

name: 献旗道
The Flag Procession Road
before: 春宴前一天，按万国商馆的老规矩，十二国的商人要扛着十二面旗，从商馆一路走到王宫南门献旗。今年走在最前头的是你们那面补了三块的旗。街口冲出来一大队国舅府的人马，戟士、弓手、铁骑，把路堵得水泄不通：「哪来的叫花子旗，也配进宫？」

The day before the spring banquet, by the Hall's old custom, merchants of twelve nations carry twelve flags in procession from the Hall to the palace's south gate to present them. This year your thrice-patched banner leads the way. At a street corner a large force of the Royal Uncle's bursts out, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, blocking the road solid. 'Where did this beggar's flag come from? Fit to enter the palace?'
after: 拦路的人被打散了，献旗的队伍走到了宫门前。宫门里立着一道纱屏，屏后坐着一个戴珠旒冠的人影。十二面旗一面面献上去，人影一面面点头，轮到你们那面补丁旗，他站了起来，深深弯下了腰，比一个王该弯的低得多。

The blockers scattered, the procession reaches the palace gate. Inside stands a gauze screen, and behind it sits a figure in a crown hung with strings of beads. The twelve flags are presented one by one and the figure nods at each. When your patched banner comes, he stands and bows deeply, far lower than a king ought to.

name: 王宫水门
The Palace Water Gate
before: 王宫临河的一面开着一道水门，从前宫里的船从这里出入。胡老大撑着他那条大船顺河漂到了水门下，可水门的铁闸被国舅府的戟士放了下来，闸上站着一排人，拿长戟往船上捅，要把这条「来路不明」的船捅沉。

On its river side the palace has a water gate where palace boats once came and went. Old Hu has poled his great boat down the river to the foot of it, but the Royal Uncle's halberdiers have lowered its iron portcullis and a line of them stand on top jabbing their long halberds at the boat to sink this 'boat of unknown origin'.
after: 戟士们掉进了河里，铁闸绞了上去。看水门的老头说，王每天傍晚都到水门上站一会儿，望着河往西去的方向，望到天黑才回。「看什么？」胡老大问。老头说：「王说，看路。」

The halberdiers end up in the river and the portcullis is winched up. The old water-gate keeper says the King comes up onto the gate every evening and stands a while looking west along the river until dark. 'Looking at what?' asks Old Hu. The keeper says: 'The King says: the road.'

name: 御厩坡
Royal Stable Slope
before: 王宫南边的坡上是御厩，养着禁军的马。国舅府的一伙骑手占了马厩，把好马都牵去了国舅府，只剩下一峰老骆驼他们牵不动：骆驼趴在地上，谁拉都不起来，屁股上烙着一个模糊的「千」字。骑手们急了，正拿鞭子抽它。

On the slope south of the palace lie the royal stables, home to the guard's horses. A band of the Royal Uncle's riders has seized them and led all the good horses off to the Royal Uncle's house, leaving only one old camel they can't shift: it lies on the ground and won't get up however it's hauled, a blurred 'Qian' branded on its rump. The riders, losing patience, are whipping it.
after: 骑手们跑了，老骆驼自己站了起来，冲你们喷了口气。老马夫说这骆驼是十年前跟着一伙外乡人来的，那伙人走的时候没带走它，王就把它养在御厩里，每天傍晚来看一回，给它喂一把豆子。「王管它叫余数，」老马夫说，「我也不懂什么意思。」

The riders flee and the old camel gets up by itself and snorts at you. The old groom says it came with a band of outsiders ten years ago. When they left they didn't take it, so the King keeps it in the royal stables and comes every evening to see it and feed it a handful of beans. 'The King calls it Remainder,' says the groom. 'Don't ask me what that means.'

name: 御膳菜园
The Palace Kitchen Garden
before: 王宫外有一片菜园，给宫里的膳房供菜，园边一溜库房。国舅府的弓手占了菜园，把库房里的东西一车车往府里运，说春宴的酒菜「由国舅府操办」。菜园的老园头被赶到了粪坑边上，嘴里还念叨着：「韭菜该割了，再不割就老了。」

Outside the palace lies a kitchen garden supplying the palace kitchens, a row of storehouses along its edge. The Royal Uncle's archers have taken it and are carting the storehouse contents off to the House by the wagonload, declaring the spring banquet 'will be catered by the Royal Uncle's house'. The old head gardener has been driven over to the dung pit and is still muttering: 'The chives want cutting. Leave them any longer and they'll go woody.'
after: 弓手们跑了，老园头第一件事是去割韭菜。他说宫里的膳房每顿都多做一份，这一份从来没人吃，撤下来就送到城门口，给排队进城的人吃，「王说，饭不能白做，碗也不能空着」。

The archers flee, and the old gardener's first act is to go and cut the chives. The palace kitchen makes one extra portion every meal, he says, and nobody ever eats it; when it's cleared it goes to the city gate for the people queuing to come in. 'The King says food mustn't be cooked for nothing, and a bowl mustn't stand empty.'
first: 库房里抄出二十筐新鲜瓜菜、十扇羊肉、四坛酸奶、一箱上好的茶砖（茶砖上印着南边茶路的字号），还有国舅府开的春宴菜单，第一道菜底下用小字注着：「红绳酒配」。

The storehouses yield twenty baskets of fresh vegetables and melons, ten sides of mutton, four crocks of yoghurt, a chest of fine tea bricks stamped with a Tea Road merchant's mark, and the Royal Uncle's house's menu for the spring banquet, with a note in small writing under the first dish: 'Serve with red-string wine.'
pass: 每次路过，老园头都从菜园里现摘一筐瓜果给你们装上，顺手塞一把刚割的韭菜：「路上包饺子。别说是宫里的，就说是我种的。」

Every time you pass, the old gardener picks you a fresh basket of melons and fruit and tucks in a handful of just-cut chives. 'Make dumplings on the road. Don't say they're from the palace. Say I grew them.'

name: 老仆摊
The Old Servant's Stall
before: 王宫下游的河湾里，一个白头发的老仆在岸边摆了个摊，卖宫里用剩的东西：蜡烛头、旧布、写秃了的毛笔，毛笔一捆捆码着，比别的东西都多。国舅府的戟士守着河湾，说宫里的人不许私卖东西，「谁买，就当谁偷」。老仆不吭声，一支支给秃笔理毛。

In the river bend below the palace an old white-haired servant keeps a stall on the bank selling the palace's leftovers: candle ends, old cloth and worn-out writing brushes, bundles and bundles of brushes, more than anything else. The Royal Uncle's halberdiers guard the bend, saying palace staff may not sell privately. 'Whoever buys is a thief.' The old servant says nothing, smoothing the hairs of the bald brushes one by one.
after: 戟士们跑了，老仆把摊上的东西随便你们挑。他每月替王擦一回冠。他说那顶珠旒冠的右边，金子上磨出了一道浅浅的槽，「像天天有一样细东西夹在那儿蹭的」。秃笔都是王用坏的，「一年三百多支，比宫里点的蜡烛还费」。

The halberdiers flee, and the old servant lets you take your pick from the stall. Once a month he polishes the King's crown. On its right side, he says, a faint groove has been worn into the gold, 'as if some slim thing rubbed there every day'. The bald brushes are all ones the King has worn out. 'Over three hundred a year. He gets through more brushes than the palace burns candles.'

name: 湖东客栈
The East Lake Inn
before: 湖东的林子边上有一家客栈，是进王城前的最后一个歇脚处。一伙国舅府的骑手住了进来，不给房钱，还把客栈的马全牵去当了坐骑。老板娘拿擀面杖守着灶房，说灶房是她的命，「骑马的进不来，骑驴的也不行」。墙上贴着一张城门的告示：「人进城，账先进城。」

On the edge of the woods east of the lake stands an inn, the last resting place before the King's city. A band of the Royal Uncle's riders has moved in, paying nothing and taking the inn's horses for mounts. The landlady holds the kitchen with a rolling pin; the kitchen is her life, she says. 'No horsemen in here. No donkey men either.' On the wall is a notice from the city gate: 'Men enter the city; the accounts enter first.'
after: 骑手们骑着自己的马跑了，老板娘把擀面杖往腰里一插，下了一大锅拉面。她说进城的人都怕城门口那位录事先生：「谁叫什么，从哪儿来，带的什么，他一眼就记住，十年前进过城的，他还记得你那天穿的什么鞋。」

The riders flee on their own horses, and the landlady tucks her rolling pin into her belt and boils up a huge pot of pulled noodles. Everyone going into the city is afraid of the clerk at the gate, she says. 'Your name, where you're from, what you carry, he remembers it all at a glance. If you came through ten years ago, he'll still remember what shoes you had on that day.'
first: 骑手们的铺盖底下抄出十袋白面、三坛葡萄酒、一筐风干的馕、两捆马料，还有他们赊账的账单：二十三天，一文未付，账单最后一行是老板娘写的「骑马的都是王八蛋」。

Under the riders' bedding you find ten sacks of white flour, three jars of wine, a basket of dried naan, two bundles of horse feed, and their unpaid bill: twenty-three days, not a copper paid, the last line written by the landlady: 'Every man on a horse is a bastard.'
pass: 每次路过，老板娘都给你们煮一锅拉面，面扯得比腰带还长，再往每人的包袱里塞两个油馕：「进了城就吃不着我的了，城里的面都是死面。」

Every time you pass, the landlady boils you a pot of pulled noodles stretched longer than a belt, and pushes two oily naan into each of your bundles. 'Once you're in the city you won't get mine. City noodles are all dead dough.'

name: 假名帖
The Forged Name Slips
before: 路边一个摊子，卖的是「名帖」：进城要在城门口报名，名帖上写好了名字、来路、货物，听说拿着它能少排三天队。卖帖的是国舅府的一伙戟士，一张帖五两银子，买的人排成了长龙。一个买了帖的老汉在城门口被退了回来，坐在摊前哭。

A stall by the road selling 'name slips': to enter the city you must register at the gate, and these slips come with your name, origin and goods already written in. They're supposed to save three days of queuing. The sellers are a squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers at five taels a slip, and the buyers queue like a dragon. An old man who bought one was turned back at the gate and sits crying before the stall.
after: 戟士们跑了，老汉拿回了他的五两银子。他说城门口那位录事先生拿着他的假帖只看了一眼，就笑了：「这帖上的数，是错的。」原来城门的名帖每一张都编了号，录事先生记得每一个号，「十年，没漏过一个」。

The halberdiers flee and the old man gets his five taels back. The clerk at the city gate, he says, took one look at his forged slip and smiled: 'The number on this slip is wrong.' Every slip at the gate is numbered, and the clerk remembers every number. 'Ten years, and he's never missed one.'

name: 画影骑
The Portrait Riders
before: 野地里一队国舅府的骑手拦住了去城门的路，领头的手里拿着一张画像，比着过路人的脸一个个看。画的是你们的旗手，旗子上的三块补丁都画上了。领头的看看画，看看你们，一拍大腿：「就是这伙！国舅说了，朝廷来的，一个都不许进城。」

A troop of the Royal Uncle's riders blocks the road to the city gate, their leader holding a portrait and comparing it face by face with everyone who passes. It's a drawing of your standard-bearer, all three patches on the banner included. The leader looks at the picture, looks at you, and slaps his thigh. 'That's them! The Royal Uncle said: nobody from the court enters the city.'
after: 骑手们跑了，画像落在了地上。画得很像，连旗手脸上的痣都点上了。画像背后写着：「探子报：一路西来，过阳关、沙海、千佛洞。」你们这一路的行踪，国舅府早就知道了；可这一路，你们也知道了国舅府的不少事。

The riders flee, dropping the portrait. It's a good likeness, right down to the mole on the standard-bearer's face. On the back is written: 'Scout reports: travelling west the whole way, through Yangguan, the Sand Sea, the Thousand Buddha Caves.' The Royal Uncle's house has known your route for a long while. But along that route, you've learned a good deal about the Royal Uncle's house too.

name: 隔市墙
The Dividing Wall
before: 城门里头本该是一条直通集市的大街，如今街中间砌起了一道新墙，砌了一半，戟士、弓手、铁骑守着工地，逼着一帮泥瓦匠日夜赶工。墙一砌完，从城门进来的人就只能绕道国舅府门前，先交钱，再进市。

Inside the gate a broad street ought to run straight to the market. Now a new wall is going up across the middle of it, half built, halberdiers, archers and cavalry guarding the site and driving a gang of bricklayers to work day and night. Once it's done, anyone coming through the gate will have to detour past the Royal Uncle's front door, pay first, and then reach the market.
after: 监工的人马退了，泥瓦匠们自己动手把墙推倒了。老瓦匠说王城有一条规矩，是现在这个王刚即位时定的：「门到市，一步不许隔。」他说那年王把这句话刻在城门里的一块石头上，石头后来被国舅搬走了，「可我们都记着」。

The overseers fall back and the bricklayers push the wall down themselves. The King's city has a rule, says the old bricklayer, made when the present King first took the throne: 'From gate to market, not one step shall be walled off.' That year the King had it carved on a stone just inside the gate. The Royal Uncle carted the stone away later. 'But we all remember it.'

name: 王城驿馆
The Royal Post House
before: 城门外的王城驿馆，原本是接待各国使者和朝廷商队的地方，如今被国舅府的家丁占了，三路人马在门前排开。管事的斜眼打量你们的旗：「朝廷？朝廷十年前就把这条路忘了。」他让人把你们的行李扔到马棚里：「上房留给国舅府的客人，你们配住马棚。」

The royal post house outside the city gate once received foreign envoys and the court's caravans. Now the Royal Uncle's household men hold it, drawn up before the door in three bodies. The steward looks your banner up and down. 'The court? The court forgot this road ten years ago.' He has your baggage thrown into the stables. 'The good rooms are for the Royal Uncle's guests. The stables are what you're fit for.'
after: 家丁们一倒，管事的换了一副脸，跪在门口，亲自把你们的行李一件件从马棚里扛进了上房，又打了热水，捧着擦脸布站在一边。驿馆的柜子里还收着十年前的住客簿，最后一页写着：「千里号三百人，住三日，账已结。」字很工整。

Once the household men are down, the steward wears a different face. He kneels at the door, carries your baggage out of the stables into the best rooms himself piece by piece, fetches hot water and stands by holding a face towel. In a cupboard the post house still keeps its guest register from ten years ago. The last page reads: 'Qianli caravan, three hundred men, three nights. Account settled.' The handwriting is very neat.

name: 候门长队
The Gate Queue
before: 城门外排着一条长队，排了好几里，有人在队里搭了帐篷，有人在队里生了孩子。队伍不动，是因为国舅府的戟士在队头卖位子，一个位子一两银，不买的往后挪。队里的人说，城门口的录事先生一天能登记几百人，「是前头这帮人堵着，不是他慢」。

Outside the city gate stretches a queue miles long. Some have pitched tents in it; one woman has given birth in it. It doesn't move because the Royal Uncle's halberdiers sell places at the head, a tael a place, and whoever won't buy gets pushed back. The clerk at the gate can register hundreds a day, the people in the queue say. 'It's this lot at the front blocking it, not him being slow.'
after: 卖位子的跑了，队伍一下子动了起来。排在你们前面的驼户说，那录事先生登记从西边来的商队时，总要多问一句：「路上……」问到这里就停住，摆摆手，「没什么，下一位」。「十年了，都这么问，」驼户说，「从来没问完过。」

The place-sellers flee and the queue lurches into motion. The camel man ahead of you says that whenever the clerk registers a caravan from the west he always asks one more thing: 'On the road...' and there he stops, waves his hand. 'Never mind. Next.' 'Ten years, always the same question,' says the camel man. 'He's never once finished it.'

name: 买名坊
The Name Buyers
before: 城北野地里一座院子，挂着「义庄」的牌子，却不收尸，收名字：国舅府的人四处打听死了的、走了的人，把他们的名字买下来，再让自己的人顶着这些名字进城。守院的戟士把一摞摞名字码在案上，像码砖头。

A compound in the open country north of the city with a sign reading 'Charity Mortuary'. It takes in no corpses, only names: the Royal Uncle's people seek out those who've died or left, buy their names, and send their own men into the city under them. Halberdiers guard the compound, stacking piles of names on the tables like bricks.
after: 守院的跑了，案上的名字一张张翻过去，都是这些年出了城再没回来的人。你们翻到一张，写着「千里号·孟小山」，旁边批着「已售」。好在城门口那位录事先生不认：顶着这个名字去的人，被他当场拦下了，「孟小山我记得，他不是这个长相」。

The guards flee and you leaf through the names on the tables: all people who left the city in these years and never came back. You turn up one that reads 'Qianli caravan. Meng Xiaoshan', marked 'Sold'. Luckily the clerk at the gate didn't accept it. The man who tried to enter under that name was stopped on the spot. 'I remember Meng Xiaoshan. He didn't look like you.'

name: 点数鼓楼
The Counting Drum Tower
before: 城墙的北角上有一座鼓楼，老规矩是每天傍晚擂鼓，当天进城几个人，就擂几下，全城的人听着数。这几个月鼓不响了：国舅府的弓手占了鼓楼，鼓槌都锯了，说「进了多少人，不用让全城知道」。城里的孩子们傍晚还是习惯性地趴在窗口等着数。

On the north corner of the wall stands a drum tower, and by old custom the drum is beaten every evening once for every person who entered the city that day, the whole city counting along. For months it's been silent: the Royal Uncle's archers seized the tower and sawed up the drumsticks. 'No need for the whole city to know how many came in.' At dusk the city's children still lean out of their windows from habit, waiting to count.
after: 弓手们跑了，你们削了两根新鼓槌，鼓楼上的老鼓手按城门送来的数擂了起来，咚、咚、咚……擂了四百一十七下，城里的孩子们跟着数，数得一个不差。老鼓手说城门的数，十年来从没跟鼓对不上过：「那录事先生的数，就是这城的数。」

The archers flee, and you whittle two new drumsticks. The old drummer beats out the number sent up from the gate, boom, boom, boom... four hundred and seventeen strokes, and the children count along without missing one. In ten years, says the old drummer, the gate's number has never once disagreed with the drum. 'That clerk's count is this city's count.'

name: 城门录事
The Gate Clerk
before: 王城的城门洞里，国舅府的戟士正推着城门要关，说「朝廷的人不许进」。门洞一侧一张小桌，桌后坐着一个人，瘦脸，眯眼，耳朵后头夹着一支笔，低头写字。那张脸，你们在千佛洞的墙上见过。有人脱口叫了声「账房先生」，他头都没抬：「客官认错人了，小的是城门录事。打完了，排队登记。」

In the gateway of the King's city the Royal Uncle's halberdiers are shoving the gates shut. 'No one from the court enters.' To one side of the passage stands a small table, and behind it sits a man with a thin face and narrowed eyes, a brush tucked behind his ear, head bent over his writing. That face you've seen on a wall at the Thousand Buddha Caves. Someone blurts out 'Master Bookkeeper!' He doesn't even look up. 'You've mistaken me, sir. I'm the gate clerk. When you've finished fighting, queue to register.'
after: 戟士们跑了，他一个个登记你们的名字。写到最后，像是随口问：「西边鬼市上，有个不说话的学徒，还在吗？」你们说他开口了，还替商队还了路钱。笔尖一顿，落下一滴墨。「那就好。进城吧。」走出门洞时，你们听见他在身后低声说：「小的这辈子，只算错过一笔。」

The halberdiers flee, and he registers your names one by one. At the end he asks, as if in passing: 'Out west in the Ghost Market, there was an apprentice who wouldn't speak. Is he still there?' You tell him the boy speaks now, and has been paying off the caravan's road money. The brush tip stops, and a drop of ink falls. 'Good. In you go.' As you leave the gateway you hear him say quietly behind you: 'Only once in my life have I got a sum wrong.'

name: 拿录事
The Raid on the Gatehouse
before: 你们进城的第二天，一大队国舅府的人马扑向城门：戟士、弓手、铁骑，说城门录事「私通朝廷」，要拿人。录事的那些簿子里记着国舅府每一个顶名进城的人，国舅等这个借口等了很久。门洞里那张小桌还摆着，桌后没有人。

The day after you enter the city, a large force of the Royal Uncle's falls on the gate, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, declaring the gate clerk guilty of 'secret dealings with the court' and come to arrest him. The clerk's registers record every man the Royal Uncle's house has sent into the city under a false name, and the Royal Uncle has long been waiting for a pretext. The little table still stands in the gateway. No one sits behind it.
after: 国舅府的人马被打退了，可录事先生不见了。桌上摊着那本登记簿，翻在你们进城那一页，每个名字后头都画了一个小小的圈。页边还多了一行字，墨迹是新的：「到。」

The Royal Uncle's forces are beaten back, but the clerk has vanished. On the table lies his register, open at the page for the day you entered, a small circle drawn after every one of your names. In the margin is one extra word, the ink fresh: 'Arrived.'

name: 内城大街
The Inner City Street
before: 从城门到王宫的大街上，家家关门闭户，街口都站着国舅府的人马，戟士、弓手、铁骑，三步一岗，五步一哨。他们说要搜一个人：瘦脸，眯眼，耳朵上夹笔的。满街的人都低着头走路，谁也不敢抬头，生怕自己长得像。

Along the street from the gate to the palace every door is shut and barred, and the Royal Uncle's forces stand at every corner, halberdiers, archers, cavalry, a sentry every three paces, a picket every five. They're searching for a man: thin face, narrowed eyes, a brush behind his ear. Everyone in the street walks with head down, afraid to look up in case they look like him.
after: 国舅府的人马被赶出了大街，门窗一扇扇推开了。卖瓜的、卖馕的又摆出了摊子，有人把耳朵上的笔拿了下来，笑着说：「这几天，全城会写字的都不敢夹笔了。」一个老头说：「那位录事先生要是真被抓了，这城的账，谁来算？」

The Royal Uncle's forces are driven from the street and doors and windows swing open one by one. The melon sellers and naan sellers set out their stalls again, and someone takes the brush from behind his ear and laughs: 'These last days nobody in the city who can write has dared tuck a brush there.' An old man says: 'If they really did catch that clerk, who'd keep this city's accounts?'

name: 搜城骑
The Search Riders
before: 城北的空场上，一队国舅府的骑手刚搜完一圈回来，个个灰头土脸。他们把城北翻了个底朝天：井里、草垛里、粪坑里都捅过了，就是找不着那个录事。领头的气得拿马鞭抽地，看见你们，眼睛一亮：「拿不着他，拿你们也行！」

On an open square in the north of the city a troop of the Royal Uncle's riders has just come back from a sweep, every face grimy. They've turned the north of the city upside down, poked into wells, haystacks and dung pits, and still can't find that clerk. Their leader is lashing the ground with his whip in fury. Then he sees you and brightens. 'If we can't take him, we'll take you!'
after: 骑手们被打散了，领头的被绑起来还在嚷：「怪了，一个大活人，能藏到哪儿去？全城都搜遍了，就差王宫没搜！」话一出口，他自己先愣住了，又摇摇头：「不可能，王宫里只有王。」

The riders are scattered, and their leader, tied up, is still shouting: 'Strange! A grown man, where could he hide? We've searched the whole city, all but the palace!' The words are no sooner out than he stops short himself, then shakes his head. 'Impossible. There's no one in the palace but the King.'

name: 传条小内侍
The Note-Runner
before: 王宫外墙下，几个国舅府的弓手围着一个小内侍，要搜他身上的纸条：他是宫里专门跑腿送条子的，这几个月城里的条子，大半是他送的。小内侍把纸条一张张塞进嘴里嚼，嚼得满嘴墨，弓手们急得直跺脚。

Under the palace's outer wall several of the Royal Uncle's archers have cornered a young eunuch to search him for notes: he's the palace's errand runner, and most of the notes going round the city these months he's carried. He's stuffing the notes into his mouth one by one and chewing, mouth full of ink, while the archers stamp in frustration.
after: 弓手们跑了，小内侍吐出一嘴纸渣，抹抹嘴。他说王每夜站着批条子，宫里没有王的床，只有一张高高的书案。登闻鼓那张「带车来见」，是他送的；给你们的最后一张，他一直揣在怀里，没舍得嚼：「东西带齐了，进宫对账。」

The archers flee, and the young eunuch spits out a mouthful of paper pulp and wipes his lips. Every night the King stands writing notes, he says; there's no bed for the King in the palace, only a tall writing desk. The 'Bring the cart' note for the Petition Drum, he carried that. The last one, meant for you, he's kept in his coat all along, too precious to chew: 'Bring everything. Come to the palace to settle the accounts.'

name: 宫前会齐
The Gathering at the Palace
before: 王宫北门外的空地上，陆陆续续聚来了一路上的人：打着结绳的老井匠、拉着旧水车的后生、赶着驼队的酒娘子、扛着旗绳的老旗官，还有撑船来的一家子。国舅府的弓手在宫墙上站成一排，冲着人群喊：「散了！聚众者，以谋逆论！」

On the open ground outside the palace's north gate, people from all along your road gather by ones and twos: an old well digger with a knotted rope, a lad hauling an old water cart, a wine woman with her camel train, an old flag officer with a halyard over his shoulder, a family who came by boat. The Royal Uncle's archers line the palace wall shouting down at the crowd: 'Disperse! Assembly will be treated as treason!'
after: 宫墙上的弓手被射了下来，人群没有散。大家把带来的东西一样样摆在宫门前：一张「第三百井」的纸条、一张借车契、二百九十九坛的收条、一根十丈长的旗绳。摆完了，谁也没说话。宫门里传出一个声音：「进来吧。账，该对了。」

The archers on the wall are shot down and the crowd stays. Everyone lays what they brought before the palace gate: a slip of paper reading 'Well 300', a cart-loan contract, a receipt for two hundred and ninety-nine jars, a halyard ten fathoms long. When it's done, nobody speaks. From inside the gate comes a voice: 'Come in. It's time the accounts were settled.'

name: 宫北门
The Palace North Gate
before: 宫门开了一道缝，门里站着一排国舅府安插进来的戟士，堵住了去正殿的路，正殿就在河边，隔着一道院子。领头的说国舅有令，春宴之前，谁也不许见王。院子那头，正殿的门开着，殿里很暗，只有一盏灯，灯下有个人影站在一张高高的书案后面。

The palace gate opens a crack. Inside, a line of halberdiers the Royal Uncle has planted bars the way to the main hall, which stands by the river across one courtyard. Their leader says the Royal Uncle's orders are that no one sees the King before the spring banquet. Across the courtyard the hall doors stand open. It's dark inside but for a single lamp, and beneath it a figure stands behind a tall writing desk.
after: 国舅府的戟士被赶出了宫门，宫里的禁军这才从各处出来，整整齐齐列在院子两边，没有一个人拦你们。老马夫牵着那峰叫「余数」的老骆驼站在院角，骆驼冲着正殿的方向，跪了下来。

The Royal Uncle's halberdiers are thrown out of the palace gate, and only then do the palace's own guards come out from all sides and line the courtyard in good order. Not one of them stops you. The old groom stands in a corner of the yard holding the old camel called Remainder, and the camel, facing the hall, kneels down.

name: 地牢逃囚
The Dungeon Breakouts
before: 王城外的荒地上，一伙衣衫破烂的人占了几间废窑，白天睡觉，夜里出来抢东西。他们是从王城地牢里逃出来的：国舅这几年把地牢塞得满满的，不交水钱的、说错话的、长得像录事的，都往里关，关多了，墙就漏了，人就一拨拨往外钻。

On waste ground outside the city a ragged band has taken over a few derelict kilns, sleeping by day and robbing by night. They're escapees from the city dungeon. These past years the Royal Uncle has crammed it full: those who didn't pay their water money, those who said the wrong thing, those who looked like the clerk. Packed that tight, the walls leak, and men keep wriggling out a batch at a time.
after: 这一拨逃囚被打散了，有的回了家，有的进了山。可地牢还满着，国舅府还在往里关人，墙还在漏，过一阵又会有一拨人钻出来，占了废窑，在夜里拦路。只要那座地牢还这么满，这里就得隔一阵来清一回。

This batch of escapees is broken up; some go home, some head for the hills. But the dungeon is still full, the Royal Uncle's house is still locking people up, and the walls still leak. Before long another batch will wriggle out, take the kilns and waylay travellers by night. As long as that dungeon stays so full, you'll have to come and clear this place every so often.

name: 收契营
The Deed-Collecting Camp
before: 城北野地里扎着一座营，国舅府的人马挨家挨户收「水契」：王城每户人家都有一张水契，写着自家每天能从渠里分多少水。他们一张契给一斗米，不卖的，就把门口的渠口用石头堵上。营里的水契已经堆了半间屋子，营外排着一溜哭哭啼啼的人。

A camp stands in the open country north of the city, the Royal Uncle's forces going house to house collecting 'water deeds': every household in the city has a deed stating how much water it may draw from the channel each day. They give a peck of rice per deed, and whoever won't sell gets the channel mouth at their door blocked with stones. The deeds already fill half a room in the camp, and outside stands a weeping queue.
after: 收契的人马被打散，水契一张张还给了各家。一个老太太捧着自家的契，说国舅这是要把全城的水攥在自己手里：「到了春宴那天，谁戴王冠都不要紧，水在他手里，城就在他手里。」

The deed collectors are scattered and the deeds handed back house by house. An old woman holding her own deed says the Royal Uncle means to hold all the city's water in his fist. 'Come the spring banquet, it won't matter who wears the crown. With the water in his hand, the city's in his hand.'

name: 水契房
The Deed House
before: 国舅府在城北开了一间「水契房」，收来的水契都存在这里，房后的库里堆着拿来换契的米。一队骑手守着门，门口贴着价目：「水契一张，米一斗；旱年，米半斗。」

In the north of the city the Royal Uncle's house has opened a 'Deed House' where all the collected water deeds are kept, with the rice used to buy them stacked in the storeroom behind. A troop of riders guards the door, and a price list is posted beside it: 'One water deed, one peck of rice. In a dry year, half a peck.'
after: 骑手们跑了，水契房的门板卸下来，契纸一张张发还给排队的人家，库里的米也分了。最后剩下一张没人来领的契，是城门边一间小屋的，户主一栏写着：「录事。」

The riders flee, the doors of the Deed House are taken off, the deeds handed back one by one to the queuing households and the rice in the storeroom shared out. One deed is left unclaimed, for a small room beside the city gate. Under 'Householder' it says: 'The clerk.'
first: 库里抄出三十斗白米、十二袋豆子、四坛清油、一箱国舅府的空白水契，还有一本收契簿，每一张都记得清清楚楚，可每一笔的米数都少写了一升。

The storeroom yields thirty pecks of white rice, twelve sacks of beans, four jars of clear oil, a chest of the Royal Uncle's blank water deeds, and a deed register, every deed clearly entered but every entry's rice a pint short.
pass: 每次路过，拿回了水契的人家都会在门口放一碗清水、一把炒豆子，你们走过，一家接一家地端出来：「水是渠里的，不收钱，豆子是自家炒的。」

Every time you pass, the households who got their deeds back set a bowl of clear water and a handful of roasted beans by their doors and bring them out one house after another as you go by. 'The water's from the channel, no charge. The beans we roasted ourselves.'

name: 假账楼
The False Ledger Tower
before: 城墙上一座角楼，楼里关着门，点着灯，日夜有算盘声。国舅府养的账房苟先生在里头造假账：要拿出一本「王城水账」，证明王这几年把城里的水都白白送给了外乡人。楼下一队骑手守着，楼梯口还拴着两条大狗。

A corner tower on the city wall, its door shut, lamps burning and an abacus clicking day and night. Master Gou, a bookkeeper kept by the Royal Uncle's house, is forging accounts in there: he's to produce a 'City Water Ledger' proving that these past years the King has given away the city's water to outsiders for nothing. A troop of riders guards the foot of the tower, and two big dogs are chained at the stairs.
after: 骑手们跑了，苟先生抱着算盘缩在墙角。他造了三个月，一本也没造成：「王的账我照着抄，抄到哪儿都对得上，水从哪口井来，到哪户去，一瓢都不差。」他叹了口气：「我这辈子头一回见着不能改的账。」他供出了国舅要在城墙上见的人：戴金面具的。

The riders flee and Master Gou cowers in a corner hugging his abacus. Three months, and he hasn't forged a single ledger. 'I copied from the King's accounts, and wherever I copied, it all tallied: which well the water came from, which household it went to, not a ladle out.' He sighs. 'First time in my life I've seen accounts you can't alter.' He gives up whom the Royal Uncle means to meet on the wall: men in golden masks.

name: 城头密会
The Meeting on the Wall
before: 夜里，城墙上一座废弃的箭楼里亮着灯。国舅府的管家坐在里头，对面是一个戴金面具的人，面具的眉心嵌着一颗红石头。楼下一队国舅府的戟士守着，门缝里漏出几句话：「金子……春宴……印……」

At night a lamp burns in a disused arrow tower on the city wall. The Royal Uncle's steward sits inside, and opposite him a man in a golden mask, a red stone set between its brows. A squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers guards the foot of the tower, and a few words leak through the crack in the door: 'Gold... the spring banquet... the seal...'
after: 戟士们跑了，管家从窗口跳下去摔断了腿，被你们捡了回来。他供出了全盘：春宴那天，红绳酒让宫里睡一夜，金面卫扮成千佛洞来献礼的和尚进宫，取了王的印，国舅当众「请王让位」。金面卫要的是金子，「千佛洞主把金面交了，这些人没交」。

The halberdiers flee and the steward, jumping from the window, breaks his leg and is picked up by you. He gives up the whole plan: at the spring banquet, red-string wine puts the palace to sleep for a night; the Gold Masks enter dressed as monks bringing gifts from the Thousand Buddha Caves and take the King's seal; and the Royal Uncle publicly 'invites the King to abdicate'. What the Gold Masks want is gold. 'The Lord of the Caves gave up his mask. These men didn't.'

name: 金面别营
The Gold Mask Camp
before: 城墙外的一段旧城根下扎着一座营，营门上挂着一排金面具，营里的弩手都戴着金面，在太阳下晃得人睁不开眼。这是千佛洞的金面卫里不肯散伙的一支，洞主交了金面以后，他们一路往西，投了国舅。领头的就是眉心嵌红石的那个。

Under an old stretch of wall outside the city stands a camp with a row of golden masks hung over its gate; the crossbowmen inside all wear gold masks that dazzle in the sun. This is the band of the Thousand Buddha Caves' Gold Masks that wouldn't disband. After the Lord of the Caves gave up his mask, they came west and joined the Royal Uncle. Their leader is the one with the red stone between his brows.
after: 金面卫败了，一个个把面具摘下来，扔在地上，叮叮当当一大堆。领头的说这些金子，是当年从窟里那三百张脸上刮下来的，「刮的时候我十九岁，戴了十年，没睡过一个好觉」。他把面具收进一只口袋交给你们：「带回去，还给那个画画的老头。」

The Gold Masks are beaten, and one by one they take off their masks and throw them down in a clanking heap. These were made, says their leader, of the gold scraped long ago from the three hundred faces in the cave. 'When we scraped it I was nineteen. Ten years I've worn it and never had a good night's sleep.' He bags up the masks and hands them to you. 'Take them back. Give them to that old painter.'

name: 国舅府
The Royal Uncle's Manor
before: 国舅府在城外的荒原上，高墙深院，院里一排排埋着水缸，比别处的水仓还多。府里最精的人马都在这里了：戟士守门，弓手上墙，铁骑绕着院子跑。国舅站在一口大缸边上，五十来岁，头发全白，看着你们：「你们以为我是坏人。我只是不想再看见这城渴死一个人。」

The Royal Uncle's manor stands on the waste outside the city, high walls and deep courtyards, rows of water jars buried in the yards, more than in any water store. His finest forces are all here: halberdiers at the gates, archers on the walls, cavalry circling the compound. The Royal Uncle stands beside a great jar, fifty or so, his hair entirely white, and looks at you. 'You think I'm a villain. I just never want to see this city let one more person die of thirst.'
after: 国舅败了，坐在缸边上，说了很久。十一年前河改了道，湖往南走，城这边旱了，他的姐姐老王后死在旱的头一年，到死嘴里都在要水。从那以后他囤水、收契、拦路，「路一开，商队来来去去，水就跟着走了」。他恨那个王：「他不是王族，来的那年正旱，是他带人把水引了回来。我囤了十一年的水，他挖了三年渠。我恨他，是因为我没做到。」他把府里水仓的钥匙交给你们：「去宫里吧，他在等你们对账。」

The Royal Uncle, beaten, sits on the rim of a jar and talks for a long time. Eleven years ago the river changed course, the lake went south, this side of the city went dry, and his sister the old Queen died in the first year of the drought, begging for water to the end. Ever since he's hoarded water, bought up deeds, blocked roads. 'Open the road and caravans come and go, and the water goes with them.' He hates that King. 'He's not of the royal blood. He came in the drought, and he's the one who brought the water back. I hoarded water eleven years; he dug a channel in three. I hate him because I couldn't do it.' He hands you the keys to his water stores. 'Go to the palace. He's waiting for you to settle the accounts.'

name: 珠旒殿
The Bead-Crown Hall
before: 正殿临着河，王城禁军三路列在阶下：戟士、弓手、铁骑，一个个站得笔直。殿上的人戴着珠旒冠，珠子一串串垂下来，看不清脸。你们把一路带来的东西摆在阶前：「第三百井」的纸条、借车契、二百九十九坛的收条、第十二根杆子的旗绳、陆字的信。王一样一样看完，抬手摘下了王冠。冠底下，右耳后夹着一支笔。瘦脸，眯眼，眼睛像在算你：是城门口的录事，是吴半壁墙上的那张脸。「十年前，」他说，「我把商队的账算错了一笔。」他把笔从耳后取下来：「账错了，要重对。禁军守了这城六年，你们打得过他们，这城的门才能交给你们。」

The main hall stands over the river, the King's guard drawn up below its steps in three ranks, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, every man ramrod straight. The figure on the throne wears a crown hung with strings of beads that hide his face. You lay before the steps what you've brought along the road: the slip of paper reading 'Well 300', the cart-loan contract, the receipt for two hundred and ninety-nine jars, the halyard of the twelfth pole, the letter signed 'Lu'. The King looks at each in turn, then lifts his hands and takes off the crown. Beneath it, tucked behind his right ear, is a brush. Thin face, narrowed eyes, eyes that seem to be reckoning you up: the clerk at the city gate, the face on Wu Banbi's wall. 'Ten years ago,' he says, 'I got one sum in the caravan's accounts wrong.' He takes the brush from behind his ear. 'A wrong account has to be gone over again. The guard has held this city six years. If you can beat them, the city's gate can be handed to you.'
after: 禁军退了，他翻开一本旧账：当年照旧图算水，图上城西有湖，他把一车水记在了湖里。可丙午年河改道，湖走了，那一车水不在了。老王借出自己的水车，他许下一年挖渠抵账，挖了三年。渠成那年老王死了，国舅要卖水，城里人求他戴冠。第四年开春，他让二百九十九人带着货先走，去赴三路的约，自己留下，抵那「尚欠一人」。六年，没有回信。他拆开陆字的信，看完笑了：「铁匣还在。」最后一页账，他写下「丝路，对毕」，把账本交给你们：「沈渡在等会算账的人。替我告诉她，我晚到了。」

The guard falls back, and he opens an old ledger. That year he reckoned the water by an old map, which showed a lake west of the city, and he counted one cartload of water as waiting in that lake. But in the Bingwu year the river changed course and the lake moved, and that cartload was gone. The old King lent his own water cart; he promised a channel within a year to repay it, and it took three. The year it was finished the old King died, the Royal Uncle meant to sell the water, and the people begged him to wear the crown. In the fourth spring he sent the two hundred and ninety-nine ahead with the goods to keep the three roads' appointment, and stayed behind himself as the 'one man still owing'. Six years, and no word back. He opens the letter signed Lu, reads it and smiles. 'The iron box is still safe.' On the last page of the ledger he writes 'Silk Road: accounts settled' and hands the book to you. 'Shen Du is waiting for someone who can keep accounts. Tell her for me: I'm late.'
